item.content:encoded:
I’m afraid this didn’t make me smile.

Additionally:

+ show block
– hide block

D-6745 (Charlie Blackwell)
Researcher Blackwell

It is never explicitly stated that D-6745 was initially a researcher, he is just casually referred to as being so in the testing logs. Why was he made a D class? That he was on the research team and drank it makes it less funny to me.

SCP-273-J will drastically lower the temperature of the individual's body parts and organs to one below 0 degrees Celsius…

Why doesn’t this read as “…organs to -1 degrees Celsius”?

However, the human still exhibits signs of life, which include a slow, rhythmic beating of the human's heart, slight movements in the human's facial region…

We’ve already been made aware that this anomaly specifically affects humans (1s line of the description’s second paragraph). So the repetitions of “human ___” are distracting and come across as clutter.

The second paragraph of the containment procedures meanders describing dehydration in numerous iterations and reads sloppily. I was hoping it was intentionally trying to be bad writing as humor but it doesn’t quite get there, and I’m not convinced from the remainder of the article that it is intentional.

only to obtain information described by the researchers as 'pure nonsense'. Following the conclusion of the interview, D-6745 proceeded to be subjected to experimentation attempting to reverse the effects of SCP-273-J.

We are told that D-6745 only spoke nonsense but see that they can determine what he is saying, which is not nonsense.

The addendum shows that the first suggestions researching reversals were provided by D-class and that strikes me as odd. (But hey it’s a J.)

There is no escalation within the first 3 attempts as all of these fluids are essentially hot/boiling water.

The kiss was a nice moment!

It’s awkward to me that poking with a hot prod was deemed too cruel (which it is!) but that pouring boiling liquids down his throat, leaving him in a tanning bed for 12 hours, put into a creamator, spit-roasted (which by the way only produces a pleasant smell if the heat is actually doing something to the skin/meat), and potentially throwing him into the sun weren’t.

Ultimately I think it just pulls off an okay concept ungracefully. What I really like here is your irl character: you clearly overcame some adversity & didn’t give up on this, so kudos for that, and it has paid off; a successful first SCP is always a big deal. Keep at it.

item.content:encoded:
Glad to see this on the mainsite! Solid +1 from me here since I've liked this since it was in the draft stage.

Results: No physical change was observed in D-6745. Carolina Reapers fished out of subject's mouth with difficulty.

This line is hilarious and sums up the premise of the SCP pretty perfectly. I remember being in chem lab and having to write overly detailed reports at the end (and we'd get docked points if we left out steps like rinsing out glassware!) and this made me chuckle because of the absurdity of the scene that would definitely be something the Foundation would still do and mention. Good mix of serious science and silly science, imho. Well done, author!
